clue.text: Closure is imminent when project leader goes

indicators.note: goes says the letter just named departs from the word

parts.note: something pending is about to happen, so 'is imminent' gives pending

indicators.note: the leader of project is its first letter

explanation.surface: A planning note: once the person heading the project leaves, it will soon be shut down.
explanation.definitionFit: A closure is a conclusion or finish, the same as a termination of something.

clue.text: Had a meal without beginning to tidy up

definitions.note: past participle, as in 'have had a meal'

indicators.note: without beginning means the first letter of the tidying word is dropped

parts.note: to neaten something is to tidy it up

explanation.surface: Someone ate their dinner but skipped the start of clearing up afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without beginning' drops the N from NEATEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Having consumed food, as in 'they have eaten', is having had a meal.

clue.text: Slut led out the most boring

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their order, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: A rude remark that a slovenly woman led the dullest people out.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of dull, which means tedious or uninteresting.

indicators.note: repaired implies the torn letters are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: Ripped notices were fixed without anyone asking anything in return.
explanation.definitionFit: An offer with no strings attached carries no conditions or obligations; the idiom means unconditional.

indicators.note: the 's stands for 'is', read as Bill is placed inside the other word

parts.note: to shed is to cast off or cast out
AD, short for advertisement, is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: A man named Bill has been thrown out, yet he was sheltered.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Bill's' is the containment signal, read as 'Bill is in'; the surface hides it as a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shaded is screened from sun or light, hence shielded.

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it
tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Learning a tango shows a dancer's bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart in the sense of spirit or nerve, as in 'take heart', is bravery.

clue.text: Children, taken aback, protect rotter for ages

indicators.note: protect means the reversed word surrounds the rotter word
taken aback reads as taken backwards, so the word for children is reversed

parts.note: seed means offspring, as in biblical usage
a cad is a rotter, a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: Startled children shield a scoundrel for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like surprise but turns the children word round to DEES; 'protect' wraps it around the rotter.
explanation.definitionFit: Decades are ten-year spans, so a long while, as in 'I haven't seen you for ages'.

indicators.note: eating means the animals word takes the offal word inside it

parts.note: deer are animals
liver is a kind of offal

explanation.surface: A rescuer of creatures that feed on innards.
explanation.definitionFit: One who delivers others from danger is a rescuer or redeemer.

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An odd, cunning person is nonetheless chic.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylish means smart and modish, in keeping with current fashion.

clue.text: Place in which Callas represented Norma, ultimately

definitions.text: Place in which Callas represented Norma, ultimately

indicators.note: represented is read as re-presented, the letters set out again in new order
ultimately points to the last letter of Norma

explanation.surface: A note on operatic history: where Maria Callas sang Bellini's Norma.
explanation.walkthrough: CALLAS plus A, the end of Norma, are rearranged; the whole clue also describes the answer, since Callas sang Norma at Milan's opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan's famous opera house was where Maria Callas performed Bellini's Norma.

indicators.note: contains means the delivery word holds the record inside

parts.note: diction is a speaker's delivery or enunciation
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A parcel delivery includes a recording of some photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A depiction is a representation or portrayal, such as an image.

clue.text: Fondness for costly staff in hospital department

indicators.note: in places the expensive-staff words inside the hospital department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
dear means expensive
men, as in workforce, are staff

explanation.surface: A complaint about a liking for expensive personnel in a hospital unit.
explanation.definitionFit: An endearment is an expression of affection, a show of tenderness.

indicators.note: backing means the word is read backwards

parts.note: avid means keen or enthusiastic

explanation.surface: Keen support for the leading lady of the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima donna is the principal female singer in an opera, a celebrated star soprano.

clue.text: The tongue can be somewhat titillating

indicators.note: somewhat signals only some of the word is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A wink: the tongue can be a little exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The tongue' looks like the body part, but it means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is a language, and tongue is an old word for a language.

parts.note: Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook = look
a round is a routine circuit, as in a milk round

explanation.surface: Examine the meat seller's daily schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a butcher's' is British rhyming slang (butcher's hook) for 'have a look'.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect a place is to survey or tour it, the phrasal verb's meaning.

parts.note: the Indus is a river of Pakistan
to try is to sample or taste

explanation.surface: Work goes into taking a sample of river water.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry means hard work or diligence, sustained exertion.

indicators.note: a variety of the letters is a different arrangement of them

explanation.surface: Show one form of trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicanery is trickery used to deceive, so it is underhand misleading.

clue.text: Various ramblers initially planted in the West Country

definitions.note: definition by example: a county within the West Country of England

parts.note: some, as in 'various people', means several

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of ramblers

parts.note: set means planted, as of seeds or seedlings

explanation.surface: A handful of hikers bedded down in south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Country is the south-west of England; Somerset is one of its counties.
explanation.definitionFit: This county in south-west England is part of the region known as the West Country.

clue.text: It is tasty but can be surpassed without a starter

indicators.note: without a starter drops the opening letter of the surpassing word

parts.note: something beatable can be outdone or surpassed

explanation.surface: A dish is delicious, yet could be bettered if you skipped the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like a first course, but it means a first letter: drop B.
explanation.definitionFit: Palatable food is fit to consume, so mildly flavoursome or acceptable.

parts.note: to char is to do housework, cleaning (as a charwoman does)
R is a map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An angler's catch from an unpolluted stream.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman) is a British cleaner; to char is to clean.
explanation.definitionFit: The charr is a trout-like freshwater fish of cold lakes.

indicators.note: in puts the runs letter inside the a-series words

parts.note: a range is a series or line, as of products
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A batsman's tally of runs in a sequence of matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' suggests runs and cricket, but it is the musical verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To score music is to orchestrate or set it for instruments, a musical sense.

clue.text: Brother rejected thanks from unruly child

indicators.note: rejected reads as thrown back, so the thanks word is reversed

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A sibling refuses gratitude from a badly behaved kid.
explanation.definitionFit: A brat is a badly behaved, spoilt youngster.

indicators.note: follows places the American after the Shakespearean

parts.note: Prospero is the magician in Shakespeare's The Tempest

explanation.surface: A wealthy US citizen is a fan of the Bard.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosperous means well-off or wealthy, thriving financially.

clue.text: Electronic device for priest? About time!

indicators.note: about means the priest letters go around the time word

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A vicar finally gets a beeper, and not before time.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager is a small electronic gadget that beeps to summon its wearer.

indicators.note: somewhat says only part of the word is used, a stretch within it

explanation.surface: Tip something over with a little too much grandeur.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it upside down or knock it over.

clue.text: Businessman in drag faces old complaint

indicators.note: faces means the first part stands in front of the old letter
in puts the business degree letters inside the drag word

parts.note: to lug is to drag or haul
an MBA, holder of a business degree, stands for a businessman

explanation.surface: A cross-dressing tycoon confronts a long-standing grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in drag' suggests cross-dressing, but 'in' is the insertion and drag is LUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint in the medical sense is an ailment; lumbago is lower-back pain.

indicators.note: in puts the person word inside the support

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar
one means a person, as in 'one never knows'

explanation.surface: Someone who backs the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in support of' reads as one phrase meaning 'pro', but 'in' is the insertion and 'of' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer leads the way, the first to explore or develop something.

indicators.note: grabbing means the wine word holds the attention word

parts.note: dry is a type of wine, not sweet
ear means attention, as in 'lend me your ear'

explanation.surface: A dull variety of wine demands notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary means dull and depressing, wearisome.

indicators.note: in places the river inside the country abbreviation

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: There really is a river in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed means in fact or truly, used for emphasis.
